title: I Finally Got My Kid a Phone
author: Chris Woolfe
summary: Chris Woolfe describes the deliberate, constraint-driven solution he arrived at for giving his nearly-ten-year-old son communication access without screens, texting, or social media: a $40 IP hotel phone configured with a VOIP account, mounted in the living room wall. His design requirements—calling only, plugged in (no battery), monitored, no browsers—reflect a coherent philosophy about what children's technology should and should not do at this age. The piece is notable for using Claude (AI) to handle the technical configuration, and for explicitly championing voice calls over texting on grounds that synchronous voice communication carries more human information. It functions as a practical tutorial and a quiet manifesto about parental intentionality with children's technology.
points: Woolfe's solution is a $40 VOIP hotel phone with a wall-mounted installation—no battery, no screen, no texting, no browser—designed to give his son calling access with none of the risks of a smartphone.
The design choice to reject texting is principled: synchronous voice calls carry tone, emotion, and intent that text strips away, and Woolfe argues families disserve themselves by defaulting to text.
The phone is plugged into the living room wall, eliminating bedroom use and bus use—a deliberate spatial constraint that functions as the primary safety mechanism.

Claude (AI) was used to configure the VOIP setup, illustrating a practical AI How-To dimension: technical configuration tasks that previously required a specialist or hours of research can be delegated to AI.

The piece implicitly argues that parental intentionality about children's technology—designing the constraints before purchasing the device—is more effective than reactive restriction after problems emerge.
quotes: We are firm believers in giving kids as much freedom as they can handle.

I've seen how kids text message each other and I think it's a shame. So much is lost in translation and frankly I think we all do ourselves a disservice when we default to texting. Calling gives so much information on tone, emotion, intent, and is also quicker than texting and more human because it is synchronous.
This phone is plugged into the wall in the living room. No texting. No screen—no browsers, no social media, nothing to worry about.
Asked Claude Fable how to configure it. Follow the instructions. Takes about 30 minutes.
Please buy your kid a regular phone so other kids can call them.
